name: Burgenwelt Ehrenberg
kurzbeschreibung: Burgenwelt Ehrenberg in Reutte: monumental fortress ensemble with 4 sites, Dem Ritter auf der Spur adventure museum, highline179 suspension bridge, and inclined elevator.
oeffnungszeiten: Ruinen 24/7 frei zugänglich; Museum täglich 09:00–18:00 Uhr (Winter 10:00–16:30 Uhr)
beschreibung:
Overview

Burgenwelt Ehrenberg, located south of the market town of Reutte in the Außerfern, is one of Central Europe's most imposing and historically significant fortress ensembles. Strategically situated along the ancient Via Claudia Augusta, the barrier complex monitored salt and goods traffic across the Fernpass on the border between Tyrol and the Allgäu for centuries. The extensive grounds combine four architectural eras into a fascinating open-air museum of military fortification: the Ehrenberger Klause in the valley, the high medieval Burgruine Ehrenberg, the early modern Fort Claudia, and the Baroque hilltop fortress Schlosskopf. Today, the complex delights visitors as a year-round attraction featuring interactive museums, inclined elevators, and the spectacular suspension bridge highline179.

History & Attractions

Its origins date back to the year 1290, when Tyrol's sovereign Graf Meinhard II. had the core castle constructed. In 1317, the Klause was built in the valley as a defensive barrier and customs station. In the 17th century, Archduchess Claudia von Medici commissioned the opposite Fort Claudia (1639–1645), before court architect Johann Martin Gumpp the Elder completed the mighty Schlosskopf fortress starting in 1703. Following military decommissioning under Emperor Joseph II in 1782, the structures fell into decay until the dedicated Burgenallianz Ehrenberg association initiated historic preservation efforts in 2001. Highlights include the interactive museum „Dem Ritter auf der Spur“ in the Klause, where visitors can explore medieval life with all their senses across 14 themed rooms. High above the valley, the 406-meter-long Tibetan suspension bridge highline179 spans the Fernpass road at a height of 114 meters, connecting the ruins' hornwork with Fort Claudia. The modern inclined elevator Ehrenberg Liner climbs 110 meters of elevation from the valley to the bridge and hornwork in about two and a half minutes.

Visit & Getting There

The historic castle ruins are freely accessible around the clock year-round and completely free of charge. The highline179 and the Ehrenberg Liner inclined lift operate 365 days a year from 08:00 to 22:00 daily. The adventure museum at the Klause opens daily in summer from 09:00 to 18:00 (in winter from 10:00 to 16:30). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): museum adults €8.00, children (ages 4–14) €4.20; highline179 suspension bridge adults €10.00, children €6.00; Ehrenberg Liner round trip €9.00 (combination tickets bridge + lift approx. €18.00). Getting there by rail: Außerfernbahn to Reutte in Tirol station, then take regional bus route 150/4250 directly to the stop Reutte Klause / Burgenwelt Ehrenberg. By car: via the B179 Fernpass road directly to the Reutte Süd / Klause exit (large visitor parking areas available, day ticket approx. €4.00).

Tips

The valley grounds with museum, visitor center, and Gasthof Salzstadl inn are exemplarily barrier-free; both the Ehrenberg Liner and the walkway of the highline179 can be used by wheelchairs and strollers (the interior of the ruin walls has gravel paths). An absolute highlight is the annual medieval festival „Ehrenberg – Die Zeitreise“ on the last weekend of July, as well as the magical light park Lumagica during winter.
